T1.implementation_approach: Use a design tool like Figma or Adobe XD to create wireframes and prototypes for the Problem Library UI. Focus on user-friendly navigation and search functionality.
T1.notes: Ensure responsive design for different screen sizes.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle CRUD operations for problems. Implement authentication and authorization for secure access.
T2.notes: Ensure proper error handling and input validation.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a relational or NoSQL database schema to store problem details, tags, and metadata. Use migrations to set up the database.
T3.notes: Optimize schema for search and filtering operations.

T4.implementation_approach: Create a form-based UI for code submission with syntax highlighting and file upload support.
T4.notes: Provide real-time feedback for input validation.

T5.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to handle code submission, validation, and storage. Integrate with the code execution environment.
T5.notes: Ensure secure handling of user-submitted code.

T6.implementation_approach: Set up a sandboxed environment using Docker or similar tools to execute user-submitted code securely.
T6.notes: Implement resource limits to prevent abuse.

T7.implementation_approach: Design a user profile page with sections for personal details, activity history, and achievements.
T7.notes: Focus on a clean and intuitive layout.

T8.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage user profile data, including retrieval and updates. Implement authentication for secure access.

T9.implementation_approach: Design a leaderboard UI with sorting and filtering options. Include pagination for large datasets.

T10.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to fetch leaderboard data based on user performance metrics. Implement caching for faster responses.

T11.implementation_approach: Design a UI for hints and tutorials with a focus on readability and accessibility. Include a search feature.
T11.notes: Use collapsible sections for better organization.

T12.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage hints and tutorials, including CRUD operations. Implement version control for content updates.

T13.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests to verify the functionality of the Problem Library. Use mock data for testing.
T13.notes: Focus on edge cases and error handling.

T14.implementation_approach: Test the code submission system by simulating various scenarios, including valid and invalid submissions.
T14.notes: Ensure security and performance under load.

T15.implementation_approach: Test user profile functionality, including data retrieval and updates. Verify authentication and authorization.
T15.notes: Check for data consistency and privacy.

T16.implementation_approach: Test the leaderboard system for accuracy and performance. Simulate large datasets to evaluate scalability.
T16.notes: Ensure sorting and filtering work as expected.

T17.implementation_approach: Test the hints and tutorials system for content accuracy and accessibility. Verify search functionality.
T17.notes: Focus on user experience and content delivery.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize SQLAlchemy instance
db_instance = SQLAlchemy()

db = db_instance  # Direct SQLAlchemy instance

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem(id={self.id}, title={self.title}, difficulty={self.difficulty})>"

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(50), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(100), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<User {self.username}>"

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    status = db.Column(db.String(20), nullable=False)  # e.g., 'Accepted', 'Wrong Answer'
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), nullable=False)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp(), nullable=False)

    user = db.relationship('User', back_populates='solutions')
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', back_populates='solutions')

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Solution id={self.id} user_id={self.user_id} problem_id={self.problem_id} status={self.status}>"

from flask import Blueprint
from app.models.solution import Solution

def solution_blueprint():
    solution_bp = Blueprint('solution', __name__)

    # Define routes for solution-related functionalities below
    
    @solution_bp.route('/solutions', methods=['GET'])
    def get_solutions():
        """
        Route to get a list of all solutions.
        """
        # Placeholder logic for retrieving solutions
        solutions = Solution.query.all()
        return {"solutions": [solution.to_dict() for solution in solutions]}, 200

    @solution_bp.route('/solution/<int:solution_id>', methods=['GET'])
    def get_solution_by_id(solution_id):
        """
        Route to get a single solution by its ID.
        """
        solution = Solution.query.get(solution_id)
        if not solution:
            return {"error": "Solution not found"}, 404
        return solution.to_dict(), 200

    @solution_bp.route('/solution', methods=['POST'])
    def create_solution():
        """
        Route to create a new solution.
        """
        # Placeholder for creating a solution
        # Logic to handle request data and save a solution would go here
        return {"message": "Solution created successfully"}, 201

    return solution_bp

# app/routes.py
# Purpose: Aggregate all blueprints
# Layer: assembly

from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

def register_blueprints(app):
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint)

from flask import Flask
from app.routes import *
from app.database import db
from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False
    
    # Initialize database
    db.init_app(app)
    
    # Register blueprints
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint, url_prefix='/problem')
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint, url_prefix='/user')
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint, url_prefix='/solution')
    
    return app

from app import create_app

app = create_app()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(debug=True)

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style competitive programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission System: A feature allowing users to submit code solutions and receive automated feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles: Profiles for users to track their progress, solved problems, and rankings.
- Leaderboard: A ranking system to display top users based on problem-solving performance.
- Hints and Tutorials: Hints and educational resources to help users learn and improve their problem-solving skills.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
